MyoKi.physical_coordinate_admission: PARTIAL and STRONG where it exists. The channel table is official and names all 18 channels in order, and this audit reproduced the raw->calibrated chain BIT-EXACTLY for channels 1-16 (max abs error 0.000e+00 deg over 83 267 samples) from `glove` + the official calibration workbook. Channels 17-18 are exactly affine but on unpublished per-participant constants. The thumb has no CMC FLEXION channel at all: channel 1 is an abduction/opposition channel and may not be substituted.
MyoKi.emg_pose_suitability: GOOD IN PRINCIPLE, NOT MEASURABLE HERE. 12 sEMG channels at 2000 Hz, 27+27 IMU channels, 24 FMG channels (subset 2) and a fully released raw glove stream, all on one time base from a common time server. But the audit holds ONE 41.6 s recording; no subject-level or task-level statement is possible.
MyoKi.downstream_task_suitability: RESTRICTED. `grasp` is a task-metadata lookup, constant over a task segment, and is NOT frame-wise ground truth.
strongest_safe_channels: the three relative abductions (cols 9,12,15) as abduction, not flexion
unsafe_channels: col 17 wrist flexion/extension - per-participant constants not published
col 18 wrist deviation - same, and no polarity is stated anywhere
col 1 'Abduction Thumb to Palm' - posture wording, no ISB name, no stated polarity, and it is NOT thumb CMC flexion
col 4 'Abduction Thumb - Index flat on table' - same objection
col 16 palmar arch - different calibration reference from every other channel
unresolved_blockers: the participant corpus (35 x 3.17-4.95 GB, 145 463 536 055 B total) is required for every subject-level claim: nothing about MyoKi generalisation is established by this audit
participant P20's EMG channels 7 and 8 are documented as detached and unusable; P05 is missing repetition 2 of task 67
the per-participant wrist calibration constants are not published, so the wrist channels can never be recovered to absolute angles
MyoKi.recommended_role: a later, SECOND external geometry source and a label-provenance stress test; not the first POC source, because the corpus is 145 GB, its labels are task-derived, and its thumb CMC flexion is absent

KIN-MUS.physical_coordinate_admission: PARTIAL. The dataset's OWN paper pins the 18-column order (Table 2) and the hand (RIGHT). 12 of the 16 canonical16 DOFs are present; all four DIPs are absent and must stay absent. Four channels are RESTRICT: the two wrists (cable artifact, envelope violation, unpublished gains, and a sign convention that conflicts across the family's own documents), the palmar arch (the group's later guide discloses the right palmar-arch gauge is malfunctioning), and the three relative abductions plus CMC1_A are semantically valid but weakly anchored. The released block is already reference-differenced and the raw gauges are not published, so the transform is TRANSFORM_NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCIBLE.
KIN-MUS.emg_pose_suitability: GOOD. The same containers carry 7 normalised and 7 raw sEMG channels; no new collection is needed for a later EMG->pose arm.
KIN-MUS.downstream_task_suitability: the phase label is the only label that passed; ADL identity is rejected
strongest_safe_channels: MCP1_F (index 2) and IP1_F (index 3) with a documented 18/22 anchor
CMC1_F (index 1) with a 22/22 anchor but only two datasets
unsafe_channels: PalmArch (index 12) - RESTRICT, malfunctioning right gauge disclosed
CMC1_A, MCP2-3_A, MCP3-4_A, MCP4-5_A - usable as abduction only, weak anchor
unresolved_blockers: the raw CyberGlove streams and the per-glove gains actually used are not published: parity can never be closed on this corpus
which of the 18 columns is the right palmar arch was never confirmed against the malfunction disclosure
KIN-MUS.recommended_role: FIRST POC TASK SOURCE for the phase label, provided the interface carries temporal state and the representation is redefined with the CORRECT index vector [1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 14, 15]

KINE-ADL.physical_coordinate_admission: DOCUMENTED BUT UNCONFIRMED. The official guide names all 36 angle columns (18 right, 18 left) in an order that DIFFERS from KIN-MUS at 8 of 18 positions, so positional mapping between the two is forbidden and an explicit semantic map is mandatory. The guide's SHA-256 equals the publisher's published hash. But the corpus was not downloaded, so no identity was confirmed against real values, and the gains actually used are not published.
KINE-ADL.emg_pose_suitability: NOT APPLICABLE - KINE-ADL carries no EMG.
KINE-ADL.downstream_task_suitability: INCONCLUSIVE. 178 elementary tasks over 2 experiments, but no trajectory was inspected.
strongest_safe_channels: the same 12 non-DIP canonical16 DOFs per hand, at MEDIUM confidence, pending value-level confirmation
unsafe_channels: WR_F / WR_A: the guide itself warns that wrist angles are missing for some subjects because of improper sensor fitting
unresolved_blockers: BE_UJI_DATASET.mat (644 185 378 B, sha256 808f0dab...) is required to confirm the column order against real values AND to resolve which 15 of the 40 (experiment, subject) keys are the same people
until SUBJECT_DATA is available, NO grouped split that crosses experiments may be constructed: 15 of 20+20 participants are shared and the overlap set is unknown
gains actually used are not published
KINE-ADL.recommended_role: a later second-hand coordination source, and the natural second dataset once the corpus is obtained; not admissible for the first POC today

tier2.recommendation: admit only if the downstream task genuinely needs the thumb; otherwise ship tier 1 alone

db9_like_failure_check.wrong_column: YES - 4 of 10 shared10 columns select a different anatomical DOF than they are named
db9_like_failure_check.wrong_sign: YES, a documentation conflict on the UJI wrist-deviation channel: KIN-MUS paper radial+, KINE-ADL paper and MOVMUS guide ulnar+. Not resolved in one direction.
db9_like_failure_check.wrong_zero: NO contradiction found. All three families state a reference posture; the UJI family uses a recorded reference posture and MyoKi a calibration posture. They are DIFFERENT zeros, so numeric equivalence is UNVERIFIED, but no zero is wrong.
db9_like_failure_check.wrong_calibration_assumption: YES, one qualified case: MyoKi channels 17-18 are on per-participant constants that are not published, and the released array does NOT use the published generic rows. Also the UJI gains actually used for KIN-MUS/KINE-ADL are the lab's placeholders in the public code.
db9_like_failure_check.subject_leakage: YES, latent, not yet realised: KINE-ADL shares 15 of 20+20 participants across experiments A and B and the overlap set lives in an undownloaded file. No split has been run, so nothing is contaminated; the hazard is that a subject-grouped split LOOKS correct and is not.
db9_like_failure_check.label_semantic_mismatch: YES, one: MyoKi `grasp` is a task-metadata lookup presented as a per-sample array, i.e. task identity relabelled, not frame-wise ground truth.
db9_like_failure_check.fake_sampling_inflation: YES, severe: MyoKi publishes every modality on one declared 2000 Hz grid while the kinematic stream changes only ~35.5 times per second - a 56.26x inflation with 98.22 % duplicated rows.
db9_like_failure_check.measured_derived_confusion: NO new case in the released arrays. All four DIPs are absent from KIN-MUS, MyoKi and KINE-ADL, and this audit proved by exact-formula test that no released column is a derived DIP. The UJI pipeline DOES derive DIP from PIP, and that derivation stays excluded from the API.
